reported.title: ADC accumulator overflows int, producing wildly wrong percent
reported.description: `sum` is declared `int` (line 11) and accumulates up to WINDOW=50 raw ADC readings (lines 54-55) before averaging at line 59. With 10-bit readings up to 1023, the sum can reach ~51150, exceeding the signed 16-bit int maximum of 32767 and wrapping negative, so `avg` and the resulting percent are garbage. The measured evidence confirms this: printed -297.7 % and -140.3 % where the injected value was 350.0 % and 500.0 % respectively, and the glitch scenario printed 162.3 % for a 150.0 % input because a single spike pushed the window sum over the limit. Firmware printed -297.7 % at 4.00 s while the injected input was 350.0 to 350.0 %: off by 647.7 % (tolerance ±3). 7 of 7 values were wrong.

reported.title: Blocking delay in button handler stretches pct: period
reported.description: The button check at lines 65-69 calls `delay(30)` every loop iteration while D5 is held LOW, and the main loop already has `delay(IDLE_MS)` (20 ms) at line 79, so each iteration takes ~50 ms instead of 20 ms. Because the pct print only occurs when the window fills (lines 57-63), the extra per-iteration delay stretches the interval between prints well beyond the 1000 ms ±150 ms budget. The measured evidence shows gaps of 1246 ms, 1337 ms and 1733 ms in the button-bounce, rapid-press and floating-input scenarios. Expected /^pct: / every 1000 ± 150 ms; 4 of 7 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 1246 ms.

judge_input.spec:
- Concentration probe on A4 at 10 mV per percent; force-sample button on D5 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Average a rolling window of ADC samples and print `pct: <value>` about once per second.
- Printed percent must stay within ±3.0 of the injected probe value.
- Lines matching `pct: ` must appear every 1000 ms ±150 ms.
- Holding D5 LOW may emit a `blend force last=<n>` note without replacing the periodic `pct:` stream.
- Every 1000 ms also print `blend batches=<n>` for batch accounting.
